paper.title_en: Dynamical thin shells in black hole ringdown
paper.abstract_en: We study how a radially oscillating thin shell outside a black hole (BH) affects gravitational wave ringdown and derive matching conditions for polar and axial perturbations from the linearized Israel junction conditions on the moving worldtube. Periodic shell motion produces Floquet sidebands in the scattered wave. For a distant shell, the motion has little effect on the prompt ringdown and only weakly modifies the late time echoes. When the shell is closer to the BH, a replica of a long lived shell mode enters the incident frequency band, increasing the late time echo amplitude by roughly two orders of magnitude. We also identify an exceptional point where two polar modes coalesce and find the contribution of its second order pole in the late time waveform.
